newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal earns 434 bln esc from selloffs in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Portugal earns 434 bln esc from selloffs in 1996.

text.p: The Portuguese government said on Tuesday it had earned 434 billion escudos ($2.9 billion) from privatisations so far this year, but this figure could increase by the end of 1996 if the government privatises tobacco company Tabaqueira.
The total so far includes 20.5 billion escudos garnered from the sale of a 13.22 percent stake in Portuguese bank Banco Totta e Acores (BTA) on Tuesday.
"With the completion of this operation, the value of privatisations conducted throughout the year has reached 434 billion escudos," a statement from the Finance Ministry said.
Under-Secretary for Finance Fernando Teixeira dos Santos said on Tuesday he hoped Portugal could sell off state tobacco company Tabaqueira this year.
The government plans to sell off a 65 percent stake in Tabaqueira, Portugal's dominant cigarette manufacturer, in 1996, according to the calendar of its privatisation programme.

Two weeks ago Economy Minister Augusto Mateus referred the privatisation of Tabaqueira to the Competition Council which had 30 days to give an opinion on the likely impact of the sale on the local market.
Mateus then has a further 15 days to consider the bids.

Candidates bidding to buy Tabaqueira are U.S. tobacco giant Philip Morris, in partnership with Portugal's Jorge de Mello group; state-owned Spanish tobacco company Tabacalera, allied to Madeira company Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos, and French group Seita.
